title: Add "Supported By Posit" badge to generics website
description:
## Overview

This PR adds the "Supported by Posit" badge to the generics website.

## Background

We've recently started adding a "Supported by Posit" badge across all Posit package websites to create a more cohesive brand presence. The badge appears on the far right of the top navigation bar or at the bottom of the hamburger menu. It links to Posit’s main website. @hadley is involved with this initiative.

The following websites already have the "Supported by Posit" badge: [ggplot2](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org), [Great Tables](https://posit-dev.github.io/great-tables/articles/intro.html), [gt](https://gt.rstudio.com), [Plotnine](https://plotnine.org), [Pointblank](https://posit-dev.github.io/pointblank/), [pointblank](https://rstudio.github.io/pointblank/), and [Quarto](https://quarto.org).

See https://posit-dev.github.io/supported-by-posit/ for more information.

## Changes

- Added a line to `_pkgdown.yml` to include the JavaScript file
- Standardized indentation in `_pkgdown.yml`

title: Testing dynamic docs
description:
Let's merge #23 first and I'll rebase this on top of the resulting master, resolving conflicts then.

This provides a testing suite for `generics` dynamic documentation by throwing a number of tests cases at `methods_rd()`.

It works by using ideas from `pkgload` and `pillar`'s testing suites:
* Loading mini-packages containing S3/S4 methods (this registers the methods)
* Running tests that check the output of `methods_rd()` against a file containing known output
* Unloading the packages

Note that I'm cheating a bit on the S4 tests on R 3.1 because `utils::methods()` only finds S3 methods there. It was only in 3.2 that it found S3 and S4 methods.

Closes #20
Closes #24

Passing travis:
https://travis-ci.org/DavisVaughan/generics/builds/439328925

title: Fix/pkgdown
description:
Two fixes for `pkgdown` to work.

1) For the `\Sexpr` blocks, we now say `rd` rather than `Rd`. `pkgdown` failed with `Rd`. This is the right way to specify the `results` section even though `Rd` works since whatever parses it does not seem to be case sensitive (maybe `pkgdown` should be more forgiving here and not be case sensitive either?).

2) When viewing development help interactively, `pkgload:::shim_help()` is being used. When this hits a method it cannot find documentation for, it errors. `utils::help()` returns a custom character object along with a message. We now use a `tryCatch()` when `shim_help()` is used, and return `character()` if no help is found. This was specifically added for the case of default methods that we export but dont document like:

``` r
library(generics)
library(pkgload)

# not an error!
help("as.factor.default", "generics")
#> No documentation for 'as.factor.default' in specified packages and libraries:
#> you could try '??as.factor.default'

str(help("as.factor.default", "generics"))
#>  'help_files_with_topic' chr(0) 
#>  - attr(*, "call")= language help(topic = "as.factor.default", package = "generics")
#>  - attr(*, "topic")= chr "as.factor.default"
#>  - attr(*, "tried_all_packages")= logi FALSE
#>  - attr(*, "type")= chr "text"

# (inside generics R Project)
# load dev generics, sorry about hard path
pkgload::load_all("~/Desktop/r/packages/generics")
#> Loading generics

# now using dev help
help("as.factor.default", "generics")
#> Error: Could not find development topic 'as.factor.default'

# and that called:
pkgload:::shim_help("as.factor.default", "generics")
#> Error: Could not find development topic 'as.factor.default'
```

I don't think this is an error on `pkgload`'s part. It's fine to throw an error. But for `generics`, we pass every method that `attr(utils::methods("as.factor"), "info")` can find through `help()` to find the path to any help docs. This is also our way of actually determining if help docs even exist. So we don't want it to error if they don't exist, we just want to handle appropriately and not include in the dynamic Rd.

title: Add some generics used by fable
description:
A few methods proposed by the [fable](https://github.com/tidyverts/fable) package have applications outside of a time series context.

---

This pull request introduces 3 new generics:

**`components()`**
Extracts components from a model or decomposition as a tidy data structure. For example, the `stats::decompose` function returns the components as a list, and using `components()` will tidy this decomposed structure into a [tsibble](https://github.com/tidyverts/tsibble). An example of extracting components from an ETS model can be found in [Model Methods/Components](https://tidyverts.github.io/tidy-forecasting-principles/methods.html#components).

**`interpolate()`**
Interpolates missing values in the response variable using a fitted model. An example of this generic can be found in [Model Methods/Interpolation](https://tidyverts.github.io/tidy-forecasting-principles/methods.html#interpolation).

**`equation()`**
Displays the mathematical representation of a fitted model. By default, returns LaTeX output suitable for usage within R Markdown documents. Proposed in https://github.com/tidyverts/fable/issues/4 and also suggested in https://github.com/tidymodels/broom/issues/492.

---

A few more generics would also be useful, although they require more consideration before including in this PR:

**`accuracy()`**
Calculates measures of accuracy for a fitted model. There is a conflict in usage between the [forecast::accuracy](http://pkg.robjhyndman.com/forecast/reference/accuracy.html) and [yardstick::accuracy](https://tidymodels.github.io/yardstick/reference/accuracy.html). Before defining the generic this inconsistency should be resolved.

forecast (and currently fable) uses a model-centric approach:

```r
library(forecast)
accuracy(ets(USAccDeaths))
#>                     ME    RMSE      MAE         MPE    MAPE      MASE
#> Training set -2.612086 262.698 202.6369 -0.08274519 2.32238 0.4634348
#>                      ACF1
#> Training set -0.007898621
```

yardstick uses a data-centric approach:

``` r
library(dplyr)
library(yardstick)
hpc_cv %>%
  filter(Resample == "Fold01") %>%
  accuracy(truth = obs, estimate = pred)
#> [1] 0.7262248
```

**`simulate()`**
The stats::simulate generic requires the `nsim` argument, and the [tidymodels conventions](https://tidymodels.github.io/model-implementation-principles/standardized-argument-names.html#numerical-arguments) suggests using the `times` argument to define the number of bootstraps, simulations and other replications.

A generic for simulate with less formals would be nice.

The current interface for simulating fable models can be found in [Model Methods/Simulation](https://tidyverts.github.io/tidy-forecasting-principles/methods.html#simulation).

title: Fix/ Support s4 and improve Rd doc output
description:
A few improvements to the last PR. When we added the speed improvements, we lost the ability to support S4 and ignore things like methods defined on an ad-hoc basis like in the global environment. This PR supports both of those now, using `methods::getMethod()` for S4.

It also improves on the Rd output, especially when there are multiple packages, by adding a header for the package that the method comes from. This is very useful for `recipes`, which loads `broom`, so you can tell which of the many `tidy` methods goes with which package.

Below is what you see when you do `?as.difftime` with `lubridate` loaded. (this is the only one where `generics` shows up because the default implementation of `as.difftime` has different args than the generic version so we added the default to the Rd).

![screen shot 2018-09-28 at 10 38 40 am](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/19150088/46215182-b810d400-c30a-11e8-9eb3-01a4b8a05959.png)

title: Remove exclusion of non-visible methods
description:
Closes #14.

I simply removed the `visible` argument altogether, since I don't think we need it anymore.

S3 methods that do not have documentation (aka no "topic") are already automatically excluded.
https://github.com/r-lib/generics/blob/master/R/docs.R#L28

title: Feature/speed up help path lookup
description:
I noticed that for functions with a large number of methods, like `tidy()`, the dynamic docs can be a bit slow (taking about 2 seconds to load when `broom` is loaded as well). This was due to repeated calls to `readRDS()` in `utils::help()` as it looped over all of the packages in the search path to find the help doc.

`utils::help()` has a `package` argument that we can use to speed it up by telling it exactly where to look for the method's help docs. This PR utilizes that, and finds the package name by using `packageName(environment(getS3method(generic, class)))`.

I'm not sure if this needs to be made more robust (support for S4?), but with `tidy()` it works great and doc loading times are much faster (down to <100 ms).

Note that this is branched from PR #14.

title: Implement coercion functions from base as generics
description:
Implements the following as generics:

* `as.factor()`
* `as.ordered()`
* `as.difftime()`

Notes:

* The generics accept `...` for extensibility.
* The generic for `as.difftime()` does not include the extra arguments (`format` and `units`) in case extensions don't need to use them.
* Because of the above point, I've included `as.difftime.default()` in the docs so the extra arguments can be seen.
